final.notes:
FINAL REVIEW, REEL 1 (01_balance_CN). I merged A and B and changed some lines. Nothing has been posted. This is for Boonchu to check.

ON-SCREEN, WHERE EACH LINE COMES FROM AND WHY
- Hook (top box, 0 to 19 s): A and B agreed, so I kept 用手撑还是用脚站 / 平衡都是一个道理. Each line is 8 characters, under the 12 limit, with no end punctuation. I took A's timing notes out of hook.en so it is only the back-translation. Unlike B, I did not repeat the hook as an entry in subs, because the editor would then burn it in twice. Burn the hook once, in the top box, from 0 to 19 s.
- Definition, 4 lines tagged to English lines 1, 3, 4 and 7 (start times 1.0 / 2.9 / 3.8 / 6.6 s, all ending at 19 s). The times use the same even-typing model both translators used: 1.0 s + 0.93 s per English line. That way each line is one phrase and no verb is cut off from its object across a line break.
  def1 瑜伽里的平衡，是清楚感知重力 (new). This joins English lines 1 and 2. It is 14 characters, exactly at the limit. The comma sits inside the line, and nothing ends the line. If the editor types it in over about 1.0 to 2.8 s, the second half arrives about when English line 2 did. A 13-character fallback is 瑜伽的平衡，是清楚感知重力.
  def2 由 bandha 引导 (new as its own line). It starts at English line 3, the same time bandha appears in the English. This fixes A's def2 (是清楚感知重力，由 bandha 引导), which is about 15 wide counting bandha as about 3, so over the limit, and which also shows bandha about 1 s early.
  def3 控制身体在各个方向的移动 (A's line, with 往……的 changed to 在……的, which is more standard). 11 characters. This avoids B's split 控制身体 / 往各个方向移动, where the verb and its object land on different lines.
  def4 不管是用手还是用脚 (new). 9 characters. This is how people say "on hands or on feet" as a tag after the main sentence. It replaces A's 无论用手还是用脚 (a dangling 无论, which reads more formal) and B's 手脚都一样 (which adds "the same" and shows it about 2 s early).
- Credit "Friday / Mysore / @boonchutanti / @missjamsai" is unchanged, with no Chinese.
- Checks passed: bandha is in Latin letters on screen; no on-screen line ends with a comma or full stop; no em dash or long dash; no 姿势, 大师, 功夫 or 上床; no asana is named, because the English names none.

POST CAPTION CHANGES
- Line 2 and 3: I split the long definition sentence in two. Line 2 says it plainly (由 bandha 来引导). Line 3 uses B's spoken 身体不管往哪个方向移动，你都控制得住 ("whichever way your body shifts, you can keep it under control") for "with control over how your body shifts in every direction".
- Line 4: I kept A's gloss 收束 (the usual Chinese yoga term for bandha) in the caption only, as the brief allows. I kept A's 下腹部. I did not use B's 小腹下方, which can read as below the belly, i.e. the pelvic floor.
- Line 6: 老师是 Boonchu 和 Jamsai. The repo lists Jamsai Tanti as an AYBKK teacher (public/bkk.html bio; bkk-api.js teacher rotation).
- Line 7: 大家各练各的，按自己的节奏来 replaces 每个人按自己的节奏，做自己的练习, which reads like a translation.
- Hashtags: 5 tags (#阿斯汤加 #阿斯汤加瑜伽 #瑜伽平衡 #迈索尔 #AYBKK; the topic tag is #瑜伽平衡) on the second-to-last line, so aybkk.net is the last line by itself. No trial offer and no call to comment.
- Each English line under the Chinese is a back-translation of the Chinese as written, not of the original English.

RISKS AND CHOICES FOR BOONCHU
1. def1 is 14 characters, right at the limit. If it looks crowded in the burn, use the 13-character fallback.
2. I added 曼谷 (Bangkok) in caption line 6. It is true (AYBKK is in Bangkok, and the reel brief says so), but the English caption does not say it. Delete it for a strictly literal version. It is not an offer.
3. The English does not say whether both Boonchu and Jamsai taught that Friday. If not, use 和 Boonchu、Jamsai 一起 instead of 老师是.
4. 各练各的 is casual. The more neutral option is 每个人按自己的节奏，做自己的练习.
5. 重力 (gravity) is the literal word. Chinese teachers often say 重心 (centre of gravity) when they talk about balance. I kept 重力 to match the English. Boonchu can switch to 重心 if he prefers.
6. I wrote 女生 (woman) for both people because the English does not say they are students. 每个人 is used for "each person".

final.notes:
How I counted: one Chinese character or full-width punctuation mark = 1. One Latin letter or space = 0.5. Every on-screen line is 14 or under. Hook lines are 9 and 7 (limit 12).

CHANGES, LINE BY LINE
Hook: line 1 is from A (够不到脚 matches "reach"). Line 2 is from B (不是你手臂太短). It speaks to the viewer and answers S8's complaint 我的手臂太短了 directly.
S1: from B (这个体式叫 / name). A had 这是 alone on a line, which looked thin. The Sanskrit name gets its own line (about 13.5).
S1b: new line, 二序列快结束时会练到 (10). A ended with 一个体式, which repeated 体式 straight after S1. B's 在二序列快结束的地方 has no verb and read like a fragment. The new line is honest to "comes towards the end of the intermediate series".
S2: from B. It is clearer that the same-side hand binds the half Padmasana foot. Line 1 is 12, line 2 about 12.5. A's 同侧半 Padmasana 的脚 was compressed and could be read two ways.
S3: from A plus 再 for "then": 另一只手再去抓另一只脚 (11).
S4: from B. 屈膝 is the normal teacher cue and reads better than A's 弯曲膝盖.
S5: changed to 听着很简单吧？ (7). The subtitle is only on screen for 0.88 s. A's 10 characters would be about 11 per second, too fast to read. B's 8 is right at the limit.
S6: line break from B (subject on line 1, verb on line 2), with A's 有意思的是. Line 1 is exactly 14. A broke the noun phrase 我遇到的 / 很多练习者 across two lines. If 14 is too tight, use 有趣的是 instead (13).
S7, S8, S9, S10: from A. For S10 I kept 觉得难 ("find it hard") instead of B's 卡在 ("stuck"), because "struggle" is broader than "stuck".
Caption line 2: split into two lines with 同侧的手, to match the audio and S2.
Caption line 8: I replaced A's line, because its English was not an honest back-translation. 要老师示范 means "it NEEDS a teacher to show you", which claims more than the source. I used B's wording, which says only that this is the kind of detail a teacher teaches on the mat.
Caption: I dropped B's 你也卡在这个体式上吗？留言说说 ("Stuck here too? Tell us in the comments"). The source does not have it and Boonchu has not approved a call to action. Add it back only if he wants one.
Caption: hashtags are on the second-to-last line and aybkk.net is the last line. There is no Bangkok trial offer and no comment call to action. #二序列 is the topic tag. #AYBKK stays in Latin letters, as in the house example.

RULE CHECK
- 体式 is used for every "pose" (hook, S1, S6, S10, caption). No 姿势, 大师, 功夫 or em dash anywhere.
- No on-screen line ends with a comma or full stop. Only S5, S9 and S10 end with ？.
- The colon in S8 is inside the line.
- All times are kept as given.
- 中级 is added once, in caption line 1 only.

RISKS
1) The 2.70 s split in S1 is an estimate (A and B both guessed). Before burning, snap it to the end of "Vajrasana" or the start of "an" in the English word captions.
2) S4 leaves out the unclear words "take the foot of straight legs" on purpose. Only the certain part is subtitled: inhale, bend the knees, roll up to sit, twist. If an editor can hear those words clearly, the line can be revised.
3) Reading speed is tight on the short subtitles: S9 is about 8 characters per second over 1.12 s, and S10 about 8.7 per second over 1.26 s. Both are within the usual 9-per-second limit. If Boonchu allows small timing changes, S5 could stay on screen until about 20.4 s, but I did not change any times.
4) 半 Padmasana follows Boonchu's spoken "half Padmasana". The proper Sanskrit, Ardha Padmasana, would push S2 line 2 to about 15.5, over the limit.
5) The hook (top) and S1 (bottom) both say 这个体式 between 0.56 and 2.70 s. This is a small repeat, but it reads as one idea: a question, then the name.
6) The caption calls Boonchu 老师 in the third person, as the source does. Switch to 我 if the account posts in his voice.
7) Nothing in the subtitles or caption describes the technique, because the video does not show it. 这里面是有技巧的 ("there is a technique to it") comes straight from the source caption.

final.notes:
Final reviewer, reel 3 (Galavasana, 36.4 s). This is a merge of A and B with a few new lines. I kept all the timings from the brief.

HOOK (top box, 0 to 7.5 s)
- Lines 1 and 2 are from A (这个高难度体式 / 靠的不是蛮力), at 7 and 6 characters. They follow the English sentence more closely and read faster than B's split (这个体式很难 / 但靠的不是蛮力), which adds a 但 that isn't in the English.
- Line 3 is new: 少用力，多呼吸 (7 characters). A's 少一点用力，多一点呼吸 (11) is correct but too long for a hook. B's 少使劲 is fine but more northern and colloquial. 用力 reads the same everywhere. Like B, I avoided 推, which on this channel means "push the floor away".
- No line ends in punctuation. The comma inside line 3 is allowed.
- I left 四两拨千斤 out of the hook to stay faithful to the on-screen English. If Boonchu wants it on screen, a tested option is 四两拨千斤 / 这个体式不靠蛮力 / 少用力，多呼吸 (5, 8, 7 characters).

TYPEWRITER (tw1 1.0 to 6.5 s, tw2 4.5 to 6.5 s, stacked like the English build)
- tw1 line 1 is new: 练高阶体式的秘诀 (8). 高阶体式 is the usual way Chinese yoga practitioners say "advanced asanas". It also stops 高级 here from being confused with the 高级A series name in the caption. A used 高阶 and B used 高级.
- tw1 line 2 is from A: 就是不要刻意去表现 (9). 刻意 carries "try to". 表现 covers both readings of "perform" ("show off" and "strive to achieve it"). B's 表演 leans only toward "putting on a show". Risk: if Boonchu meant only "don't strive", use 就是不要刻意去完成.
- tw2 is from A: 但还有一件事 ("but there's one more thing"). It's a more natural teaser than B's 但还有别的, which sounds unfinished in a flat way. The ending stays open and nothing answers it.
- The English trailing ".." is dropped, because of the line-end punctuation rule.
- Layout risk: from 1.0 to 6.5 s the 3-line hook box and up to 3 typewriter lines are on screen together, which is 6 Chinese lines. The typewriter lines should sit over the English typewriter area and must not touch the hook box. If it looks crowded, end tw1 at 4.5 s so that only tw2 shows from 4.5 to 6.5 s.

LABELS
- label_d is 二序列 + 三序列 口令课 (about 10 characters). This changes A's 引导课 to B's 口令课, the standard term in mainland Ashtanga studios (paired with 迈索尔 for Mysore). I used it in the label, the caption and a hashtag. I didn't add 中级/高级, to keep the label short.
- label_e is AYBKK 广州工作坊. Both translators had this.
- The Galavasana label (8 to 14.5 s) has no Chinese and no sub entry, so the name isn't burned twice. The @boonchutanti and @missjamsai stickers are left alone. The teacher's count has no words to subtitle.

POST CAPTION (line by line)
1. Taken from B's structure with 一个 added: 这是 Galavasana，三序列（高级A）里的一个体式. This reads more naturally than A's 出自. 高级A appears once, in brackets.
2. One sentence: 一排同学…停留，再回到头倒立. I used 同学 rather than 学员, because it is warmer and is how Chinese studio teachers refer to students. 停留 is the standard yoga word for "hold". "Lifts back up" is rendered 回到头倒立, back-translated honestly as "goes back up to headstand". I didn't write Sirsasana, because the English doesn't name the headstand variation (in Advanced A it may be Sirsasana II).
3. B's 老话说得好. Chinese readers don't need "中国有句老话", which sounds like it's explaining China to foreigners.
4. New: 小小的巧劲，胜过很大的力气. 巧劲 is the natural spoken word for "smart force". A's 小而巧的力，胜过大力 sounds stiff, and B's 一身蛮力 overstates "a big one" and repeats 蛮力 from line 6.
5. A's 高难度体式也是这个道理.
6. Both translators had this: 靠的是你的关节和呼吸，不是蛮力. It is straight from the source.
7. A's spoken form, changed to 口令课.
8. 老师报数 is new. 报数 is the natural phrase for calling the count. A's 数口令 is an odd collocation, and B's 数数 sounds childish.
9. B's 没有人一开始就练这个. It is more spoken than A's line and means the same.
10. 从一序列开始，一天一天练上来. This is A's version with the subject left out, which is natural in Chinese and implies a general "you". B's 慢慢 was dropped as padding that isn't in the source.
11. 5 hashtags: #阿斯汤加 #阿斯汤加瑜伽 #AYBKK #四两拨千斤 (topic) #口令课.
12. The last line is aybkk.net only.
- The caption uses normal Chinese punctuation, because the no-end-punctuation rule applies only to on-screen lines.

CHECKS
- No em dash or long dash anywhere.
- 体式 throughout, never 姿势.
- No 大师 or 功夫.
- Sanskrit name in Latin letters.
- Every on-screen line is within the limit: hook 12 characters or fewer, subtitles 14 or fewer, 2 lines or fewer per subtitle.
- No on-screen line ends in a comma or full stop.
- No Bangkok trial offer, no price, and no comment call to action.
- No facts, numbers or quotes beyond the English source. Galavasana being in Advanced A and the entry from headstand match the house rules and the Ashtanga sequence.
- Every English line under the caption is a back-translation of the Chinese chosen, not of the source.
